findings.title: Harness diagnostics live in the application contract package while every consumer bypasses its package boundary

evidence.note: The application shared package defines a tool-id and harness-diagnostics transport contract.
Drift analysis reaches directly into packages/shared/src instead of using a supported package export.
The lint-ratchet adapter repeats the source-relative coupling from another ownership area.

evidence.measurement: 11 non-test TypeScript consumers directly import packages/shared/src/schemas/harness-diagnostics.js; pinned git grep found zero client/server runtime consumers.
evidence.note: The contract is entirely tooling-owned despite its application-layer home.

findings.problem: A harness-only protocol is owned one layer away from every real consumer. Harness, analyzer, and lint tools consequently depend on a repository-relative source location, while moving or extracting the harness requires application-package changes.
findings.proposedDirection: Move the envelope to a tooling-owned contract module or small workspace package with a stable export, then migrate harness, drift-ai, logs-audit, and lint-ratchet together.

priorPackOverlap.novelty: The landed harness cluster unified diagnostic helpers but did not address the schema's application-package placement or the surviving direct source imports.

findings.title: Logging producers and their auditor separately encode the same protocol

evidence.note: The server defines redaction values, sensitive query parameters, and Pino redaction paths.
The auditor independently defines accepted redaction values, sensitive keys, field paths, query parameters, and URL aliases.
The producer owns closed authz event, reason, and outcome vocabularies; mutation and broadcast variants continue at lines 94-136.
The auditor duplicates the authz, mutation, and broadcast outcome vocabularies.

findings.problem: Adding a sensitive spelling or structured-event outcome requires synchronized edits in the server and its certification tool. The auditor is intended to police the producer, but currently shadows its policy, leaving authority and drift behavior unclear.
findings.proposedDirection: Extract a neutral structured logging-policy module that distinguishes producer paths, normalized audit aliases, sensitive URL parameters, event families, and allowed outcomes; derive both sides from it.

priorPackOverlap.novelty: H19 extracted logs-audit-local types; it did not unify the server producer contract with the audit policy.

findings.title: Database URL selection is duplicated across server tests, E2E, root diagnostics, and devcontainer setup

evidence.note: Server test support owns TEST_DATABASE_URL and DATABASE_URL-derived test-database precedence.
E2E setup independently implements E2E_DATABASE_URL, TEST_DATABASE_URL, and DATABASE_URL fallback rules.
The root diagnostic implements separate test and E2E resolvers and explicitly says it mirrors the test harness.
Devcontainer provisioning mirrors the URL-to-name and fallback rules again in shell.

findings.problem: One database-selection contract spans root tooling, server test internals, E2E configuration, and shell provisioning. A contributor changing an environment variable or fallback must discover multiple copies, and the operational command imports a test-only module to recover one constant.
findings.proposedDirection: Extract a pure environment-parameterized test/E2E URL resolver behind a supported tooling boundary. Reuse it from Playwright, global setup, db-status, and server test setup; expose a narrow CLI result for shell provisioning.

findings.title: Human-readable server messages act as client control-flow contracts

evidence.note: The client classifies invite failures through case-sensitive substring matches on server prose.
Distinct CONFLICT reasons are represented only by their independently authored messages.
The page branches on the exact character-not-found message.
Account deletion contains two additional exact or substring message branches.

findings.problem: Changing capitalization or improving server copy can silently degrade invite, character-load, and account-deletion flows to generic errors. Contributors must discover an undocumented prose protocol because generic tRPC codes do not distinguish the domain reasons.
findings.proposedDirection: Add stable domain reason codes to application errors and centralize client narrowing. Keep human-readable messages presentation-only and migrate the three evidenced flows as a bounded first set.

findings.title: A generic mutation acknowledgment is hidden under auth while weaker domain copies drift

evidence.note: Auth owns the broadly reused `{ success: literal(true) }` contract.
Link and unlink redeclare weaker `{ success: boolean }` contracts.
Inventory defines another domain-local boolean acknowledgment.

evidence.measurement: 14 production router files reference successResponseSchema, measured with pinned git grep.
evidence.note: The auth-named schema is already a cross-domain primitive.

findings.problem: New contributors must know that an auth module owns a repository-wide response primitive, while nearby domains expose subtly weaker copies. Endpoint contracts therefore depend on which definition a contributor happens to find.
findings.proposedDirection: Move or canonically alias the acknowledgment from a neutral shared response module and converge the weaker copies, retaining domain-specific type aliases only where they improve vocabulary.

priorPackOverlap.novelty: The shared-schema cleanup left three measured acknowledgment stragglers and the misleading auth ownership.

findings.title: Shared weapon helpers force server persistence projections through double assertions

evidence.note: getWeaponDataFromItem requires a complete InventoryItem while reading only itemType, name, and properties.
The server deliberately queries narrow Prisma-facing item and proficiency shapes.
Those projections are widened through `as unknown as` assertions to satisfy the shared helper signatures.
Client callers naturally possess complete wire entities, explaining why the over-broad signature is convenient in only one layer.

findings.problem: Rules helpers are coupled to transport entities rather than the minimal data they compute from. Server code must pretend partial Prisma rows are fully validated wire entities, obscuring the real boundary and coupling unrelated schema changes to attack resolution.
findings.proposedDirection: Define structural helper inputs containing only the fields used, derive the server participant shape from its Prisma selection, and remove the assertion bridges.

priorPackOverlap.novelty: The landed weapon work addressed representation behavior, not the helper's public dependency surface or surviving server assertion boundaries.

findings.title: Adding a homebrew entry type requires synchronizing seven parallel inventories

evidence.note: The shared enum defines the entry-type vocabulary.
A separate exhaustive shared record maps the same keys to schemas.
The client repeats the key set in EntryFormByType and repeats it again in the editor registry at lines 162-216.
Filter labels and plurals live in another non-exhaustive array.

findings.problem: The schema and editor maps are type-checked, but create and filter option arrays can omit a new entry type without an error. Labels, plurals, ordering, schemas, and editors also lack an obvious canonical inventory.
findings.proposedDirection: Keep validation schemas in shared, but establish one exhaustive client metadata registry keyed by HomebrewEntryType and derive cards, creation options, filters, form typing, and editor lookup from it.

findings.title: Code-intel excludes declared workspaces while hard-coding application topology repeatedly

evidence.note: The Bun workspace includes packages/*, tools/*, and examples/lint-ratchet-demo.
Code-intel defines its workspace as only shared, server, client, and scripts.
Queries reject files outside those fixed application and scripts directories.

evidence.measurement: 127 tracked TypeScript files under tools/ and examples/lint-ratchet-demo are excluded, counted at the audit pin with git ls-tree and rg.
evidence.note: Declared workspaces cannot be targeted by the contributor-facing code-intel command.

findings.problem: A tool named around workspace analysis silently means only three application packages plus scripts. The supported topology is also repeated across discovery, project creation, caching, resolution, and result bucketing.
findings.proposedDirection: Create one project inventory derived from root workspace and tsconfig metadata. If application-only scope is intentional, rename the abstractions and emit an explicit supported-scope diagnostic.

priorPackOverlap.novelty: The open code-intel slices concern a context bag and cache abstraction; this is a separate root-workspace coverage mismatch with 127 excluded files.

findings.title: Local lint rules lack one canonical registration catalog

evidence.note: Every local rule is manually imported and paired with its string id.
Only meta.docs fields are projected; rule identity, source, invocation, and enforcement mode remain separately authored.

evidence.measurement: 32 kind=lint-rule controls repeat rule identity, source path, and enforcement command, counted from the manifest at the audit pin.
evidence.note: The second inventory is large enough to make new-rule registration a recurring synchronization ritual.
The generator already discovers rule metadata and ratchet registrations programmatically.

findings.problem: Adding a rule requires creating the module, editing a static plugin map, choosing normal-lint or ratchet activation, and repeating its identity and invocation in the harness manifest. Drift checks catch omissions later but do not provide one obvious authoring surface.
findings.proposedDirection: Introduce a typed rule catalog or generated static registry owning id, module path, and enforcement mode once; derive the plugin map and lint-rule controls from it.

priorPackOverlap.novelty: The landed work single-sourced rule documentation fields but left identity, source, invocation, and enforcement mode duplicated.

findings.title: Repository-path containment has several incompatible local dialects

evidence.note: A write-oriented codemod resolves, relativizes, checks a broad `startsWith("..")`, and adds an extension rule.
Analyzer tooling defines separate isInside and isSameOrInside semantics.
Harness projection uses a stronger normalized, lexical, symlink, and physical-containment contract.

evidence.measurement: At least five distinct containment implementations were located across codemods, code-intel, harness projection, and shared Git utilities using pinned git-grep searches.
evidence.note: The implementations differ on root acceptance, separator boundaries, normalization, and symlinks.

findings.problem: Tools answer the same containment question differently, so contributors cannot tell which contract is reusable and fixes to path semantics must be rediscovered across ownership areas.
findings.proposedDirection: Provide two deliberately named primitives in scripts/lib: lightweight lexical containment for read-only analysis and hardened repository-target resolution for writers. Migrate callers according to semantics.

priorPackOverlap.novelty: H14 unified normalization inside path-policy only; this evidence spans codemods, code-intel, harness projection, and Git utilities.

findings.title: Magic-item seed validation shadows shared category and rarity contracts

evidence.note: Shared exports the complete magic-item category and rarity enums.
The seed module repeats both literal lists in private schemas with the same names.
The duplicated validators are embedded in the raw seed-input schema.
A neighboring seed path already imports shared spell contracts.

findings.problem: Adding or renaming a category or rarity requires synchronized edits in two packages with no type-level relationship. Drift is costly because the seed validates checked-in data while API paths validate against the other copy.
findings.proposedDirection: Import the shared magic-item category and rarity schemas into the seed module while retaining the deliberately seed-specific outer object shape.

findings.title: The generic SRD getAll contract is a client-specific lookup read model

evidence.note: The server explicitly selects five collections and fields for useSrdLookups.
The partial cross-layer bundle is exposed through the generic getAllOutputSchema name.
The client converts the endpoint response into its actual lookup-map read model.
The named hook is the endpoint consumer and the reason for its selection shape.

findings.problem: The endpoint is neither all SRD data nor an explicitly named lookup bundle. Server selection, shared schema, and client maps must evolve together, but the generic name encourages contributors to treat it as a general aggregate.
findings.proposedDirection: Preserve the batched request but name and document a stable SRD lookup-bundle read model in shared, then type the hook directly from it.

priorPackOverlap.novelty: This keeps routers/srd.ts intact and addresses the cross-layer read-model name rather than reopening the refused content-family split.

findings.title: Authentication redirects depend on undocumented dual-prop precedence

evidence.note: AuthGuard supplies both `to` and `href` to Navigate and explicitly requires href to win.
GuestGuard repeats the convention and adds a stand-down branch to avoid overwriting the destination.
The real-router regression spec documents the precedence as an implementation detail that dependency upgrades may change.
Unit tests use a local Navigate stub that exposes both props but cannot validate real-router precedence.

findings.problem: A core authentication flow carries duplicate destination representations and relies on unusual framework precedence. The contract is discoverable only through long comments and an E2E regression, making normal router maintenance hazardous.
findings.proposedDirection: Give the login route a validated returnTo search contract and use typed router navigation. Encapsulate dynamic post-login navigation in one real-router-tested adapter.

findings.title: Repository command meaning changes silently with the current working directory

evidence.note: At the root, dev starts the repository workflow and build composes all packages.
Inside shared, the same vocabulary means package-local TypeScript work.
Inside server, dev starts only the server and root gates disappear.
The repository explicitly documents that root-only commands fail from package directories because Bun selects the nearest package.json.

findings.problem: The same-looking command can start one package, watch only types, build everything, build one package, or fail depending on shell location. This is a code-side new-contributor tripwire repeated across all workspace packages.
findings.proposedDirection: Provide a stable repository dispatcher that resolves the Git top level from any subdirectory and use it as the human-facing entry point for repository workflows; retain package scripts as explicit implementation surfaces.

findings.title: Validate concrete homebrew entry data before submission

evidence.note: Shared already exports an exhaustive entry-type-to-Zod-schema registry and validator.
The client already maintains an exhaustive type-correlated editor registry.
Submission validates only the opaque outer create or update input.
A rejected mutation is reduced to a generic retry message instead of field feedback.

findings.problem: DMs and players authoring homebrew must submit invalid concrete data, wait for a server round trip, and still receive only a generic failure. The feature is cheap because exhaustive shared validation and client editor registries already exist.
findings.proposedDirection: Run the shared per-type schema before mutation and translate issue paths into the existing fieldErrors map, while retaining authoritative server validation.

findings.title: Make notifications navigate to the campaign context already encoded in their payload

evidence.note: Notification payloads already carry campaignId and messageId.
Offline-whisper notifications populate both target identifiers.
Clicking a notification only marks it read; payload data is ignored.
The campaign route already supports validated tab deep links.

findings.problem: DMs and players must read a notification, close the popover, locate its campaign, and select the relevant tab even though the notification already identifies the destination. Payloads, producer wiring, and addressable campaign tabs make the missing navigation inexpensive.
findings.proposedDirection: Map notification types to destinations, marking read and navigating campaign-accepted notices to overview and offline whispers to the chat tab. Message anchoring can remain separate.

priorPackOverlap.novelty: Prior work stabilized Notification.data; this feature consumes those identifiers rather than changing the schema.

findings.title: Add the campaign ownership transfer that account deletion already promises

evidence.note: Account deletion instructs owners to transfer or delete their campaigns.
The client repeats that transfer instruction.
Campaign settings expose deletion but no ownership transfer.

evidence.measurement: A pinned production search for campaign ownership transfer found only the server/client instructional messages and no mutation or UI action.
evidence.note: The instructed alternative does not exist.

findings.problem: A DM with other campaign members cannot delete their account without destroying the campaign, despite being told transfer is available. Owner identity, member roles, authorization helpers, and campaign mutation infrastructure already make the addition comparatively bounded.
findings.proposedDirection: Add an owner-only mutation that transactionally promotes a selected member and updates ownerId, then expose it beside the campaign danger zone.

findings.title: Expose a machine-queryable harness provenance view

evidence.note: Contributors currently follow a manual checklist across smoke tests, path policy, package scripts, the manifest, and prose references.
The validator already materializes manifest and generated-surface relationships.
Changed-path-to-smoke relationships are already computed as structured data.

evidence.measurement: The 2,859-line manifest contains source, invocation, verify-slot, generated-surface, hook-wiring, and skill-wiring facets.
evidence.note: Most graph inputs exist; only a supported joined query is missing.

findings.problem: Contributors and harness users must manually correlate a large manifest, package scripts, generated Markdown, and path-policy output to learn why a path triggers a check or where a control runs. Existing typed readers and relationship data make a provenance query relatively cheap.
findings.proposedDirection: Add a read-only text/JSON query by path, control id, or package-script name that returns connecting controls, checks, generated outputs, slots, hooks, and source locations.

findings.title: Let users rename a homebrew collection while importing it

evidence.note: The E2E page object must compare hidden hrefs because imported and original collections have no visible discriminator.
The client parses the typed envelope but submits its original collection name unchanged.
Persistence copies the envelope name directly into the new collection.
Cards show name, visibility, and author but no import provenance.

findings.problem: Re-importing a private collection produces visually indistinguishable cards, forcing even E2E helpers to use internal URL identity. DMs and players exchanging or backing up homebrew benefit, and the existing envelope already accepts a renamed collection.
findings.proposedDirection: After parsing, present the collection name in an editable “Import as” field and submit a copied envelope containing the chosen name.

findings.title: Enable the existing comment-density sensor for scripts with narrow exceptions

evidence.note: Scripts and eslint-rules are first-class analyzer roots.
The comments check nevertheless excludes both trees wholesale.
The detector already excludes tests, fixtures, declarations, and configurable prefixes.

evidence.measurement: 570 tracked source-like files are hidden by the two configured prefixes after excluding the detector's default tests, fixtures, declarations, and fixture-named files.
evidence.note: The broad exclusions remove ongoing coverage from large tooling surfaces.

findings.problem: Harness users and contributors receive no automated comment-density signal for 570 tooling files and must repeat manual audits. The detector and its report-only calibration already exist, making narrower exceptions inexpensive.
findings.proposedDirection: Replace blanket scripts and eslint-rules exclusions with a small list of generated, vendored, or deliberately prose-heavy exceptions, initially retaining advisory behavior.

bugsSideList.title: Campaign description controls cap valid input at half the shared contract limit
bugsSideList.whySuspectedBug: Shared campaign validation accepts descriptions up to 10,000 characters, while both browser controls hard-cap input at 5,000.

bugsSideList.title: Duplicate homebrew entry names can bind imported references to an arbitrary entry
bugsSideList.whySuspectedBug: The envelope and database permit duplicate type/name entries, while import builds an overwriting name-to-id Map from an unordered query and uses it for subclass and background references.

bugsSideList.title: Date-only campaign and note values may display one day early west of UTC
bugsSideList.whySuspectedBug: Date inputs are serialized at UTC midnight and later rendered with local-time toLocaleDateString, allowing negative UTC offsets to display the preceding calendar date.

bugsSideList.title: Several path-containment predicates reject valid in-repo names beginning with two dots
bugsSideList.whySuspectedBug: The predicates use relative.startsWith(".."), so a valid child such as `..generated/file.ts` is treated as outside; scripts/lib/git.ts uses the separator-aware boundary.
